tip: For feelings and states, use estar com plus a noun. Tô com preguiça is literally I'm with laziness, meaning I feel lazy.
Portuguese takes breakfast rather than has it: 'tomaram café da manhã' uses the same tomar you use for drinks.

target: Não esquenta a cabeça com isso.
tip: Esquentar a cabeça literally is to heat the head and means to worry. Não esquenta a cabeça = don't stress about it.

target: Pois é, a vida não é fácil.
tip: 'Pois é' is a common filler/agreement expression meaning 'yeah' or 'exactly' or 'that's how it is.' Used to show empathy or agreement.
'Oxe' is an exclamation from Northeastern Brazil expressing surprise or confusion. It's spread across the whole country.
'Tomara que' means 'I hope that' and is followed by the subjunctive. But you'll hear it so often, you'll learn it as a set phrase.
Tô ligado literally means I'm switched on, and as slang it means I'm aware or I got it. Tô ligado = understood.
'Dar certo' is one of the most important Brazilian expressions. It means 'to work out/to go well.' 'Vai dar certo' = it'll be fine.
'Pera aí' is a contraction of 'espera aí' (wait there). Very common in casual speech.
'Faz parte' means 'it's part of life' or 'it happens.' 'Vida que segue' = life goes on. Together, they form a very Brazilian philosophical acceptance.
Gente usually means people, but gente boa describes one kind, decent person. Você é gente boa = you're a good person.
Adjectives usually follow the noun, so it is 'emprego novo', not novo emprego.

target: Eu tô de saco cheio disso.
tip: Estar de saco cheio is a mildly crude idiom for being fed up. Tô de saco cheio disso = I'm sick of this.

target: A gente comeu demais no rodízio.
tip: 'Rodízio' is a Brazilian dining style where servers bring endless rounds of meat (or pizza, sushi, etc.) to your table. Very popular.

target: Eu notei que ele estava nervoso.
tip: que (that) can't be dropped: notei que ele estava = I noticed [that] he was. English can omit it.

target: Ele trouxe comida para todo mundo.
tip: Trouxe is the irregular past of trazer (to bring), not a regular ending. Ele trouxe comida = he brought food.

english: Poor thing, he doesn't deserve that.
tip: 'Coitado/coitada' means 'poor thing.' Used to express sympathy. It's not rude – it's genuinely empathetic.

english: Can I ask you a question?
tip: Fazer uma pergunta pairs fazer (to make) with pergunta to mean ask a question. Posso te fazer uma pergunta = can I ask you a question.

english: I've got my eye on you!
tip: Estar de olho em means to keep an eye on someone. Tô de olho em você = I'm watching you, as a playful warning.

english: He found out the truth yesterday.
tip: 'Saber' past: ele soube. The past of 'saber' often means 'found out' – a completed discovery.

target: Nós almoçamos juntos na sexta passada.
english: We had lunch together last Friday.
tip: 'Almoçamos' is the same for present and past (nós form). Context tells you which tense: 'ontem almoçamos' = past, 'sempre almoçamos' = present.

target: Que vergonha, eu esqueci o nome dele.
english: How embarrassing, I forgot his name.
tip: Dele is de + ele and means his. O nome dele = his name. Portuguese puts the owner after the noun.

target: Ele parou de fumar há seis meses.
english: He stopped smoking six months ago.
tip: 'Há' before a time span means ago, so 'há seis meses' means six months ago.

target: Ele fez questão de pagar o jantar.
english: He insisted on paying for dinner.
tip: 'Fazer questão de' means to insist on, literally to make a point of, so 'fez questão de pagar' means he insisted on paying.

target: A gente chegou atrasado por causa do trânsito.
english: We arrived late because of traffic.
tip: 'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: 'a gente chegou', never chegamos.

target: A gente fez uma pausa para o café.
english: We took a break for coffee.
tip: 'A gente' means we in casual speech but takes a singular verb, like ele: 'a gente fez' = we did.

english: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.
tip: 'Pode deixar' means 'leave it to me' or 'don't worry about it.' It's a very reassuring Brazilian expression.

english: Did you go to the concert yesterday?
tip: 'Ir' past: vocês foram. 'Foram' is past of both 'ir' and 'ser' – context tells which. Here: 'went.'

target: Eu dei uma olhada no cardápio.
english: I took a look at the menu.
tip: 'Dar uma olhada' means to take a quick look: 'dei uma olhada no cardápio' = I glanced at the menu.

target: Eu mudei de ideia sobre a viagem.
english: I changed my mind about the trip.
tip: Portuguese changes of something: 'mudar de ideia' means change your mind, and the de is required, like mudar de casa.
